title: pcell cost balance replicates on seed 3: cy=0 yield rises to 1.52 while cells collapse 24 -> 5; cy=0.03 holds 28 cells at yield ~1.0-1.09 with deaths at the 2nd percentile and selected splits
summary: Fresh seed 3 with the author's genealogy.py to t=100000. cy=0: mean yield 1.13 (t=25000), 1.32 (50000), 1.52 (100000); cells 24 -> 11 -> 5; 48 mature deaths at mean yield percentile 0.075 (48/48 below the median); splits unselected (0.45, 5/13 above); parent-daughter r 0.87. cy=0.03: yield 1.00, 1.03, 1.09; cells 26, 29, 28; 37 deaths at percentile 0.022 (37/37 below); splits at 0.64 (19/26 above); r 0.95. A short labkit pack of the cy=0.03 world (t=3000) shows walled cells condensing from the particle soup by t~800.

observations.F: data/summary.txt: cy0 yield 1.52, cells 5, deaths at 0.075, splits 0.45; cy0.03 yield 1.09, cells 28, deaths 0.022, splits 0.64; rerun_cy003/sheet.png

controls_run.F: the cost scan itself: cy=0 vs cy=0.03 on seed 3 (data/real_cy0_s3.log, data/real_cy003_s3.log)

verdicts.limitation: I did not re-run the inert-trait twin or cy=0.06/0.1. The labkit pack covers only t=3000. As in my review of the multilevel claim (20261025T0840), the death percentile measured at death is largely built during each cell's life, so the death differential overstates selection on the inherited trait.
